actions.q: What is the Coverdell ESA contribution limit?
actions.target: What is the Coverdell ESA contribution limit?

fact_basis.fact: For 2025 the total of all contributions to all Coverdell ESAs for one beneficiary can't be more than $2,000 (from all sources); the $2,000 limit is unchanged on this page
fact_basis.source: https://www.irs.gov/publications/p970 (Coverdell ESA, "Limit for each designated beneficiary")

fact_basis.fact: MAGI $95,000-$110,000 (single) / $190,000-$220,000 (joint): the $2,000 limit is gradually reduced; at $110,000 / $220,000 or more you can't contribute
A Coverdell ESA can be held for a beneficiary who is under age 18 or is a special needs beneficiary
fact_basis.source: https://www.irs.gov/publications/p970 (Coverdell ESA, "Who can have a Coverdell ESA?")

actions.task: Extend the existing FAQ answer: state the MAGI phase-out range ($95,000-$110,000 single, $190,000-$220,000 joint; no contributions at or above the top) and that contributions are only allowed for a beneficiary under 18 (or special needs). Keep the $2,000 figure; 3-4 sentences total.

actions.q: What happens to a Coverdell ESA if my child does not go to college, and can I roll it to a Roth IRA?

fact_basis.fact: Distributions not used for qualified education expenses are taxable (earnings) and generally carry a 10% additional tax on the amount included in income
fact_basis.source: https://www.irs.gov/publications/p970 (Coverdell ESA, "Additional Tax on Taxable Distributions")

fact_basis.fact: 10% additional tax exceptions: distribution after the beneficiary's death, because the beneficiary is disabled, or to the extent of a tax-free scholarship/educational assistance

Not taxable if rolled over (within 60 days) to another Coverdell ESA for the same beneficiary or a family member under age 30; the beneficiary can also be changed to a family member under 30 with no tax
fact_basis.source: https://www.irs.gov/publications/p970 (Coverdell ESA, "Rollovers" and "Changing the Designated Beneficiary")

fact_basis.fact: A contribution to a 529 (QTP) on behalf of the Coverdell beneficiary (or, after a beneficiary change, a family member) is a qualified education expense
fact_basis.source: https://www.irs.gov/publications/p970 (Coverdell ESA, "Contributions to a qualified tuition program (QTP)")

fact_basis.fact: The SECURE 2.0 rollover to a Roth IRA is described for long-term 529 plans (QTPs) only, in the same publication; the Coverdell rollover rules name only another Coverdell
fact_basis.source: https://www.irs.gov/publications/p970 (QTP "Rollover to Roth IRA" reminder vs Coverdell "Rollovers")

fact_basis.fact: Page text: funds generally must be used by age 30 or are distributed with tax and 10% penalty on earnings
fact_basis.source: this page, FAQ "Does a Coverdell have to be used by a certain age?"

actions.task: New FAQ answering the three PAA questions (cash out / child skips college / Roth IRA): leftover can go to a family member under 30 via rollover or beneficiary change, or into a 529 for the same beneficiary; cashing out pays income tax on earnings plus 10% except for death, disability or scholarship; the 529-to-Roth rule does not apply to a Coverdell (rolling a Coverdell into a 529 first is not described by the IRS as a Roth route). No Roth promise. Practical tone, short.
